newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to privatise some defence firms by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to privatise some defence firms by 1999.

text.p: The Portuguese government expects to privatise part of its defence industry during its current mandate ending in 1999, Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino said on Tuesday.
Asked if the government would sell off some defence activities during its present four-year term, Vitorino told Reuters in a brief conversation: "Most certainly."
He was speaking on the sidelines of a presentation to launch Portugal's pavilion at the Lisbon 1998 Expo World Fair.

The Portuguese government said this month that it had decided to set up a commission to restructure the defence industry which is expecting a loss of three billion escudos ($20 million) in 1996 after a loss of 4.1 billion in 1995.
The commission should present a plan including the establishment of a holding company for the defence firms and the possible privatisation of firms not directly engaged in producing arms.
Portuguese state defence firms produce bullets, grenades and automatic weapons as well as military equipment.
Portugal's ambitious privatisation programme could bring in at least $450 million to state coffers this year and a similar sum in 1997, officials said.
